html:
The Jagiellonian University in Kraków was founded on 12 May 1364 by King Casimir III the Great as the Kraków Academy, the second university in central Europe after Prague's.

It faded after his death and was refounded in 1400 with money left by Queen Jadwiga, wife of Władysław Jagiełło, from whom it later took its name. In the 1400s it was known for astronomy and mathematics, and Copernicus studied there from 1491. In November 1939 the Nazis called its professors to a lecture and sent them to concentration camps, an attack on Polish learning. Teaching went on in secret during the war. Pope John Paul II studied there too. Its Collegium Maius is the oldest university building in Poland.
sum: The Jagiellonian University in Kraków was founded on 12 May 1364 by King Casimir III the Great as the Kraków Academy, the second university in central Europe after Prague's.
